input.summary:
room-17 (bedroom 3) is written but places nothing: its whole 294-cell box (x37..43, y11..16, z43..49) is already claimed as air by the mansion shell, so all 28 writes are refused.
The OFF-PALETTE check reports nothing, since every block id it uses is in palette.json, but that check only runs on writes that are accepted, so it has not been exercised.
I did not edit room-17.mjs: clearing the REFUSED line would mean deleting the furnished room, and the actual fix is in parts/shell.mjs, which I was told not to touch.
left: REFUSED 28 is not fixable inside room-17. parts/shell.mjs:26-27 fills every room interior with explicit air (fill(..., "air")), and runParts counts an air write as owned, so every cell of bedroom 3 is locked before this part runs. Room-17 placed 0 blocks; the 294-cell box has zero free cells. Moving the writes is impossible, and removing them would clear the line but delete the whole furnished room. Not done without your say-so.

The fix belongs in parts/shell.mjs: stop writing air into room interiors (a fresh grid is already air there, so the fill adds nothing), or leave interior cells unwritten. Then room-17 lays its bed, barrels, fence, stairs, lanterns, carpet and chain as designed, with no further change to this file. That is the change I'd recommend.
Every room part shares this blocker: the shell's interior air fills lock all rooms, so every room reports 0 placed. Not checked beyond room-17.

OFF-PALETTE is not yet verified. The palette check runs only on accepted writes, so it never ran for room-17. Reading palette.json by hand, all nine ids it uses are present (white_bed, barrel, dark_oak_fence, dark_oak_stairs, dark_oak_slab, red_carpet, lantern, candle, iron_chain), so nothing needs swapping.
make.sh still writes build.nbt, but room-17 contributes no blocks to it. The part is not built.

waste.what: Finding out which earlier part owned the refused cells: I ran the build with MCD_PARTS_CELLS, then wrote a node script to compare the owner of each room cell against the room's box.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and a 294-cell scan
waste.tool: runParts should name the owning part when a write is refused ("x,y,z owned by mansion shell as air") and warn when a part placed 0 with refusals, instead of printing only the first 8 refused cells.

waste.what: Establishing that the whole room box was claimed. The refusal line showed 8 of 28 cells and said nothing about the rest, so the total lock had to be inferred from placed 0 plus a box scan.
waste.tool: A `mcd claims build.nbt --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` command that lists, per part, how many cells in a box it owns and whether any are free, would have answered this in one call.

waste.what: The off-palette check is skipped for refused writes, so it reported nothing for room-17 even though its blocks were never checked. I checked the palette by reading palette.json by hand.
waste.cost: one manual check of nine ids
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette check before the lock check, so refused writes still get palette-checked and the report is complete.

waste.what: Deciding whether removing the writes was the right fix. Removing them would clear the line but delete the room, so the choice is a judgement call the tool cannot make.
waste.cost: a reasoning step, no tool call
waste.tool: A `--dry-run` for runParts that reports, per part, what would be refused and what would land, so a fix can be tested before editing.
